name: csv
description: RFC 4180 CSV parsing and stringifying. Parse mode turns raw CSV text into rows (arrays, or objects when a header row is present), handling quoted fields, escaped quotes, CRLF/LF line endings, embedded newlines inside quoted fields, and ragged rows (reported in warnings instead of throwing). Parsed rows are capped at 20,000 (truncated:true if the source had more). Stringify mode turns rows back into CSV text, quoting only fields that need it and always terminating the last line, so a trailing all-empty row round-trips correctly. Use this instead of naive string.split(',') whenever the CSV might contain quoted commas, quoted newlines, or escaped quotes.

mode.description: "parse" turns CSV text into rows; "stringify" turns rows into CSV text.

text.description: Raw CSV text. Required for mode "parse".

rows.description: Rows to serialise. Required for mode "stringify": either an array of arrays, or an array of uniform objects.

columns.description: Stringify: explicit column order/subset for object rows, or a header row to prepend to array rows.

delimiter.description: Field delimiter. Defaults to a comma.

header.description: Parse only: treat the first row as a header and return objects keyed by (deduplicated) column name. Defaults to false.

rows.description: Parse: array of arrays (no header) or array of objects (header:true).

columns.description: Parse with header:true: the (deduplicated) column names, in order.

warnings.description: Non-fatal issues found while parsing: ragged rows, deduplicated header names.

truncated.description: Parse only: true if the source had more than 20,000 data rows and the result was cut to the first 20,000.

text.description: Stringify: the resulting CSV text. Always terminated with a trailing line ending.
